attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: "Will be known as" is a firm forecast that 2025 will be seen in hindsight as the peak and the confidence turning point. The "may go up" concession belongs to the next sentence and is handled in the companion claim.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: hindsight recognition of 2025 as the speculative peak and the start of sustained loss of confidence, with later nominal highs allowed. No deadline was given, so only a durable reversal plus independent retrospectives can resolve it.

evidence.note: The Week, 26 Oct 2026, before the cutoff. It reports investors reassessing AI and a live crash-versus-soft-landing debate. That is an ongoing debate, not a retrospective naming 2025 as the peak.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The only evidence shows ongoing reassessment and debate in October 2026. No durable broad reversal and no convergent retrospective naming 2025 as the peak are documented, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own summary statement in his post.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation about AI company profitability and technical moats as of late 2025. The Nvidia exclusion is kept. Whether it also covers the moat clause is ambiguous, and the contract flags this.

contract.note: The ordinary reading (net profit, "few" as a small minority) is fair. But the result depends on interpretations the speaker did not supply: which companies count, the Q3 2025 window, and whether Nvidia is excluded from the moat clause.

evidence.note: Palantir's Q3 2025 release (a company disclosure) shows it was profitable. One profitable firm cannot refute "few" when no population is defined.
Morningstar analyst view (Aug 2025) that Nvidia has strong switching costs. This bears on the moat clause only if Nvidia is not excluded from it, and it is an analyst judgment.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no defined population of AI companies and no count of how many were profitable. It has no evidence across companies on technical moats. One profitable firm and an analyst's view on Nvidia's moat neither establish nor refute the claim. Unresolved.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: a broad, durable unwinding of AI valuations, later recognised as beginning with the September 2025 Oracle episode. Oracle-only declines are correctly treated as not enough.

evidence.note: Dec 18, 2025, before the post. Documents Oracle's 46% drop from its Sept 10 high, the episode Marcus refers to. Cannot show the later sector-wide outcome.
Kiplinger, Mar 2026. Oracle remained weak but analysts rated it Buy. This concerns one company and shows no broad unwinding.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The evidence covers only Oracle's own decline and continued analyst optimism about Oracle. Nothing documents a durable broad AI valuation unwinding or retrospectives naming September 2025 as its start. Unresolved.
